subjects.label: Factions and their demands
subjects.description: The political groups and communities in the city, what they demand, managing their favour, their rallies and protests, and loathing particular ones such as the Pilgrims; not the council vote or the laws themselves.

subjects.label: Council and laws
subjects.description: Passing laws through the council: the votes, the laws on offer such as child labour, mandatory reproduction, prisons or martial law, and what signing them leads to; not the factions who cast the votes.

subjects.label: Child labour
subjects.description: Sending children to work, above all in the mines, as the law the game offers and players joke about accepting; not other harsh laws or general cruelty.

subjects.label: The Steward's standing
subjects.description: How the city treats its Steward: being blamed for the dead, voted out or exiled by your own people, or seizing absolute power and becoming Leader under martial law; not exiling factions or ordinary law-making.

subjects.label: Unrest, exile and force
subjects.description: Riots and protests and how the player puts them down: exiling factions or rioters to the Frostland, calling in guards and the military; not the Steward's own exile.

subjects.label: Compared with the first game
subjects.description: Weighing the sequel against its predecessor: whether it is a continuation or a different game, what was expanded, what was lost, and whether fans of the first should buy it; not comparisons with other games or genres.

subjects.label: Macro scale instead of individuals
subjects.description: The move from managing individual buildings and people to districts and whole-city systems, and whether that larger scale loses the personal survival feel; not general praise or complaint about the mechanics.

subjects.label: Districts on the hex grid
subjects.description: Laying out districts and hubs on the hexagonal grid, which district goes where, and tools or complaints about the hex layout; not the broader scale shift from the first game.

subjects.label: Deluxe edition extras
subjects.description: The deluxe edition and pre-order: the promised DLC, the digital novel and art book, and regret over having paid for them; not the base price or general DLC policy.

subjects.label: Real-world political parallels
subjects.description: Reading the city through real ideologies and places: building communism, a Stalin ending, oil and American democracy, life in Norilsk, whether the game is woke; not the in-game factions themselves.

subjects.label: The cold and freezing
subjects.description: The frozen world as the subject itself: jokes about freezing, citizens dying of cold, snow and winter as the setting; not the mood it creates or how it looks.
